questions.stem: The force that opposes the relative motion of two surfaces in contact is called:
questions.explanation: Friction — arises due to microscopic irregularities and molecular attractions between surfaces. Types — static (before motion begins, up to a maximum), kinetic (during sliding), rolling (smallest). Friction is useful (walking, braking) but also wasteful (heat losses in machines). Reduced by lubrication, ball bearings and streamlining.

questions.stem: The product of mass and velocity of a body is called its:
questions.explanation: Momentum p = m × v. Unit: kg·m/s. Momentum is conserved in an isolated system — the basis of rockets, recoil, collision analysis. Kinetic energy is ½mv² (scalar, unit joule). Force — rate of change of momentum (Newton's 2nd law: F = dp/dt = ma for constant mass). Acceleration — rate of change of velocity.

questions.stem: The upward force exerted on an object immersed in a fluid is called:
questions.explanation: Buoyancy — the upward push a fluid exerts on a submerged / floating object. Archimedes' Principle: the buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid displaced. An object floats if it is less dense than the fluid (ice on water), sinks if denser. Surface tension is the elastic skin of a liquid surface (water-striders walk on it). Viscous force opposes motion through a fluid (honey is more viscous than water).

questions.stem: The force needed to keep an object moving in a circular path is directed towards the:
questions.explanation: Centripetal force — always directed towards the centre of the circular path. Magnitude F = mv²/r. Sources of centripetal force differ — tension in a string for a swung stone, gravitational pull for a satellite, static friction for a car on a curve, normal force for a bicyclist banking on a turn. 'Centrifugal force' is a pseudo-force experienced in the rotating frame.

questions.stem: The SI unit of pressure is the:
questions.explanation: Pressure = Force / Area. SI unit — pascal (Pa) = 1 N/m². Atmospheric pressure at sea level ≈ 101,325 Pa = 1013.25 hPa. Common units — bar (10⁵ Pa), mmHg / torr, psi. Newton is force; joule is energy; watt is power. Pressure cookers, hydraulic brakes, blood-pressure cuffs and weather forecasts all use pressure measurements.

questions.stem: An object with a mass of 10 kg on Earth is moved to the Moon. Its weight on the Moon is approximately (taking Moon g = 1/6 of Earth's):

options.option_text: Zero, because there is no atmosphere

questions.explanation: Mass is the amount of matter (invariant, 10 kg here). Weight = mass × g. On Earth — g = 9.8 m/s², so weight ≈ 98 N. On the Moon — g ≈ 9.8/6 ≈ 1.63 m/s², so weight ≈ 10 × 1.63 = 16.3 N. This is why astronauts can jump much higher on the Moon. 10 kgf is a force unit (~98 N) — effectively the Earth-weight value, not the Moon-weight value.

questions.stem: Newton's third law of motion states:

options.option_text: For every action there is an equal and opposite reaction
A body at rest stays at rest unless acted on by a force
Energy can neither be created nor destroyed

questions.explanation: Newton's 3rd law — action-reaction pairs of forces act on two different bodies, are equal in magnitude, opposite in direction. Examples — rocket propulsion (exhaust pushed down → rocket pushed up), swimming (arms push water back → water pushes swimmer forward), walking (foot pushes ground back → ground pushes foot forward). 1st law — inertia. 2nd law — F = ma. Energy conservation is a different principle (1st law of thermodynamics).
